subject: Re: Proposed edits — IP, training rights & feedback license
messages:
From: Claire Hsu <claire.hsu@bluewave.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>; karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Danielle Lopez <d.lopez@bluewave.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial redlines on MSA and Order Form

Hi Naomi / Karthik —

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Legal attached their high-level redlines to the MSA and the Order Form — main asks are around: output ownership, a broad training/data use carveout, and a perpetual feedback license.

See attachments (BlueWave_redline_MSA_v2.docx, Annotated_OrderForm_BW.pdf). We're hoping to get to a short set of compromise options rather than an all-or-nothing clause swap. Specific asks:
- Customer ownership of generated outputs for customer inputs (including derivative works)
- No use of Customer data for model training without explicit opt-in and a commercial benefit clause
- Feedback/telemetry may be used only in aggregated, non-identifiable form unless Customer opts in

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a narrow feedback license and a 90-day retention window for raw request logs?

Claire
Legal — BlueWave Analytics

--

Attachment: Annotated_OrderForm_BW.pdf (pdf, 76 KB)

From: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>

Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial redlines on MSA and Order Form

Claire —

Appreciate the redlines and clear priorities. High-level response while we loop in Legal:
- Output ownership: Redwood's standard position is to grant customers ownership of outputs generated from their inputs; we'll confirm exact language but OK in principle.
- Training/data use: we do not train models on customer-provided private inputs by default. We ask for a limited feedback license to improve the service (non-identifiable, aggregated). We can make that revocable and narrow in scope.
- Retention: 90 days for raw per-request logs is workable for many customers; we can offer a 12-month audit log export for compliance on request (with additional fees).

I'll put Markus (legal) and Aditya (privacy/engineering) on copy to draft specific language and a limited counterproposal.

Proposed next step: legal-to-legal redline exchange and a short call Monday to align. Does 10am PT work for BlueWave?

Thanks,
Naomi
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

--

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Claire Hsu <claire.hsu@bluewave.com>, Danielle Lopez <d.lopez@bluewave.com>

Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 08:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Redwood counterproposal (tracking changes attached)

Hi Claire / Danielle —

Thanks for the clarity. Attached is a short counterproposal and a redline of the MSA focused on three paragraphs: Output Rights (Section 3.2), Training & Model Improvements (Section 5.1), and Feedback License (Section 5.2). Key points in our draft:

1) Output Rights: "Customer retains all right, title and interest in Outputs generated by Redwood in response to Customer Input, subject to Redwood's limited right to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for service improvement."

2) Training & Model Improvements: "Redwood will not use Customer Input or Outputs to retrain or improve models without Customer's prior written opt-in; opt-in may be scoped by dataset, team, or product feature."

3) Feedback License: "Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, revocable, worldwide license to use Feedback (as defined) solely to operate and improve Redwood services; such use shall be limited to aggregated, non-identifiable data unless Customer grants explicit permission for other uses."

We also proposed a 90-day window for retaining raw request logs with the option to extend to 12 months for compliance exports at an agreed fee.

See attached: BlueWave_Redwood_Counter_MSAv1.docx (redline). Happy to walk Legal through line-by-line — Naomi, can you coordinate a slot Monday 10am PT if that still works?

-Karthik
Senior Sales Counsel, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: BlueWave_Redwood_Counter_MSAv1.docx (docx, 95 KB)

From: Claire Hsu <claire.hsu@bluewave.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: BlueWave Legal <legal@bluewave.com>, Danielle Lopez <d.lopez@bluewave.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 09:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood counterproposal (tracking changes attached)

Karthik / Naomi —

Thanks for the swift counter. A few clarifying points from Legal:
- The Output Rights clause looks OK but they want an explicit carveout ensuring Redwood cannot use Outputs to create a competing product feature (narrow non-compete language).
- For Training & Model Improvements, they will only agree to opt-in if there is an explicit commercial benefit (e.g., a credits/incentive program) and an audit trail for any data used.
- For Feedback License, they asked that any telemetry used be expressly defined and that IP derived from aggregated telemetry be disclaimed from Redwood ownership (i.e., aggregated improvements not create standalone IP claim over Customer-specific patterns).

They are open to the 90-day raw log retention if we provide a straightforward mechanism to request immediate deletion for specific datasets.

Would Markus be able to propose specific alternative wording around "competing product" carveouts and auditability? If we can get proposed language in writing, Legal will likely accelerate.

-C

--
Attachment: (none)

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Claire Hsu <claire.hsu@bluewave.com>, BlueWave Legal <legal@bluewave.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 12:01:00 -08:00
Subject: Proposed carveout and auditability language

Claire —

We appreciate the specificity from BlueWave Legal. Proposed language to address the competing product and auditability concerns (excerpt below). Full redline attached if you want to drop into your doc: 

- Competing Product Carveout (new subclause): "Notwithstanding any other provision, Redwood shall not use Customer Inputs or Outputs to develop or train a model or feature that is intentionally designed to replicate or replace a Customer product or service that is materially similar to Customer's publicly offered product lines at the time of the Input."

- Auditability & Opt-in Recordkeeping: "If Customer opts in to allow Redwood to use Customer data for model improvement, Redwood shall maintain an auditable record (dates, datasets, anonymization steps) and provide Customer with a quarterly summary on request. Any datasets used for training will be subject to the parties' mutually agreed data handling procedures and may be exported for Customer audit within 30 days of written request."

We also clarified that aggregated telemetry improvements are expected and that Redwood disclaims ownership of Customer-specific IP embedded in Customer Inputs/Outputs.

If BlueWave wants a formal SLA around deletion requests for narrow datasets we can include a 30-day turnaround SLA for deletion confirmation.

If the language below looks reasonable, we can produce a clean MSA / Order Form for signature and a short addendum describing the opt-in credits program (commercials to be agreed).

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

--

Thanks all — that wording is very helpful. BlueWave Legal asked me to confirm two items before we proceed to signature: 

1) Formal description of the opt-in commercial benefit (can Redwood provide a short addendum draft outlining credits or service discounts tied to training opt-in?)
2) Confirmation of the 30-day deletion confirmation SLA for specific dataset removal requests and the mechanics for an export for audit (format, delivery channel).

If you can send a 1-page addendum and the mechanics today, Legal will greenlight the clean MSA/order form and we can move to DocuSign. Proposed signing window: end of week.

Best,
Danielle Lopez
Procurement, BlueWave Analytics
